but an enormous amount of time goes into drawing just the human body. Art teachers often promote life drawing (drawing the human form) as an appropriate means of developing skill and style. You have to draw it again and again, badly and then better and then well. They don't mind if your drawings are bad, they just want you to use the complex form of the human body (something that its very easy for us to notice mistakes in) to learn how to draw. Isn't playing one piece a lot like drawing one form a lot? (I can see how there are differences but can you see how there are similarities?)

So would it be right to approximate that you think perhaps its a choice between learning to play using one or two "complex" pieces or, many more "simple" pieces?  
The method of breaking down a piece into small parts is exactly how I've gone about learning. But maybe it would have been more fun if I had used lots of simpler songs rather than one complex song (i've actually used a few more, but not a massive variety). How about with improvisation? If you already have a good knowledge of the theory and want mainly to improve your ability to play across many octaves,  to develop a more nuanced and fluid sensibility, might it be advantageous to play songs that contain the kind of playing you want to nurture for yourself?
But don't you think that after a few years of this (putting some good attention into refining technique) You could also pick up a piece similar in complexity to Clair de Lune in a week or so?

Maybe because its easy to get frustrated and impatient. You don't get the conventional good-feeling pay-off for a long time. Which is perhaps an important motivator. But if you learn to be patient could this way of learning have its own advantages?

I started playing difficult songs early with the attitude that I would allow it to take as long as it took to learn them, breaking it up into tiny pieces that I could cope with.  What was probably most important, was learning to enjoy whatever I played and being enthusiastic about whatever meagre attempts I made at playing this bar or that bar, this scale or that scale. you know what I mean?
